land.text: the south-western Britons: Cornwall, Devon and west Somerset

predecessors.note: The Dumnonia page gives no founding year; it dates the kingdom 'between the 6th century CE and the 7th century CE'. 602 is Cliopatria's. After Deorham (577) 'the Britons of Dumnonia' were 'cut off by land' from Wales.

land.text: the rump kingdom in what is today Cornwall

successors.note: Cliopatria starts a Cornwall row (4,538 km2) in 710. The page says that after Egbert's campaigns of 813-822 there was 'a rump state in what is today called Cornwall' and that the last known Cornish king, Donyarth, died in 875.

land.text: Wessex's 710 shape, 9,588 km2 larger than its 705-709 shape: Devon and the rest of the Dumnonian shape outside Cornwall

successors.note: The page does not date the West Saxon take-over of Devon: 'c. 936 ... Athelstan ... evicted the Britons from Exeter and the rest of Devon'.

capitals.name: Tintagel
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Isca Dumnoniorum (Exeter) (before c. 400) Tintagel'. The page gives no years for Tintagel; 602-709 is a bridge.

correction.text: Cornwall, Devon and Somerset: 'the kingdom of Dumnonia covered Cornwall, Devon and parts of west Somerset', with eastern and central Somerset British until Peonnum

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 602-657: before Cenwalh's victory the Britons held more of Somerset than Cliopatria's shape. 'Cenwalh advanced west through the Polden Hills to the River Parrett, annexing eastern and central Somerset' (Peonnum page); 'the eastern part of Dumnonia' was annexed by Wessex 'around 658' (Dumnonia page). Natural Earth's 'Somerset' leaves out Bath and North Somerset, which Wessex took at Deorham in 577.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 658-684 only; the border with Wessex is the River Parrett

keyframe_review.note: 602-704 in Cliopatria, 14,349 km2 (lat 49.98-51.31, east edge lon -2.87, about the River Parrett). The Dumnonia infobox has no area. Years: the shape is the Dumnonia of 658-684, when the Parrett was the border ('the Parrett remained the border until 681-685'). Before 658 see dumnonia_602b; from 685 see dumnonia_685, which removes Somerset.

correction.text: Dumnonia without Somerset: Cornwall and Devon after the West Saxon advance to the Bristol Channel

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 685-704: after 'until 681-685' Wessex held 'western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel' (Peonnum page), so Somerset leaves the shape. The correction removes Somerset from the Cliopatria outline; what is left is Cornwall, Devon and the coast, my reading of the page's 'western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel'.

705-709 in Cliopatria, 14,349 km2, the same outline as 602. The shape is corrected as dumnonia_685 (without Somerset). 'In 710 Geraint was defeated in battle by King Ine of Wessex' and Cliopatria's Cornwall row begins in 710, so 710 belongs to the Cornwall shape; Aldhelm wrote to 'its king Geraint regarding the date of Easter' (c. 705).

region.text: Cornwall, Devon and parts of west Somerset

ledger.note: 602: Cliopatria's Dumnonia begins. The page gives no founding year; it says the kingdom 'existed in Sub-Roman Britain between the 6th century CE and the 7th century CE' and that Gildas wrote of the ruler Constantine of Dumnonia.

region.text: eastern and central Somerset, east of the River Parrett

ledger.note: c. 658: Cenwalh of Wessex takes eastern and central Somerset. 'in 658 his army met the Britons for a climactic battle at Peonnum' (the infobox says 'about AD 660'); he 'advanced west through the Polden Hills to the River Parrett, annexing eastern and central Somerset', 'modest in size'; the Dumnonia page: 'the eastern part of Dumnonia being permanently annexed by Wessex'. The site of Peonnum is uncertain.

region.text: western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel

ledger.note: By 685: Wessex reaches the Bristol Channel. The Parrett 'remained the border until 681-685', when Centwine's victory let the West Saxons occupy 'western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel'. The page gives a span, not a year; 685 is its end.

region.text: Devon, the part of the Dumnonian shape outside Cornwall

ledger.note: 710: Cliopatria cuts Dumnonia to Cornwall. The page says only 'In 710 Geraint was defeated in battle by King Ine of Wessex'; it does not say Devon changed hands then (it dates the rump state in Cornwall after Egbert's campaigns of 813-822 and has Athelstan evict the Britons from Devon c. 936).

710: the kingdom of Dumnonia gives way to a Cornish rump. The page gives no end date for Dumnonia ('a gradual process') and the year is the battle of Geraint against Ine; Cliopatria's Cornwall row (710-946) continues the Britons of the south-west.

wars.name: Battle of Peonnum

zones.text: eastern and central Somerset to the River Parrett

wars.outcome: Cenwalh's West Saxons beat the Britons and annexed eastern and central Somerset as far as the Parrett, which stayed the border until 681-685.
wars.note: The Peonnum page says the battle was 'fought about AD 660', gives 658 in the text, and never names Dumnonia; the Dumnonia page equates the Britons of Somerset with Dumnonia. The site is uncertain (Penselwood is only a place-name suggestion).

wars.name: West Saxon advance to the Bristol Channel

zones.text: western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel

wars.outcome: Centwine of Wessex wins and the West Saxons occupy 'western Somerset up to the Bristol Channel'.
wars.note: The page's wording on the Britons' leader is confused (it names Cadwaladr of Gwynedd); it is read here only for the dates and the land.

wars.name: Ine of Wessex against Geraint
wars.outcome: 'In 710 Geraint was defeated in battle by King Ine of Wessex.' The page does not say what land changed hands.
wars.note: Zones left empty: the Dumnonia page says only 'In 710 Geraint was defeated in battle by King Ine of Wessex' and names no land (it has Athelstan evict the Britons from Exeter and the rest of Devon c. 936); the ledger's 710 loss of Devon is Cliopatria's (confidence 1). Later: 722 a British victory at Hehil (Annales Cambriae), 813-822 Egbert, 838 Hingston Down; these belong to the Cornwall dossier.

certainty.note: Only the Parrett frontier of 658-685 is named on the pages; the rest is approximate.

sources.title: Dumnonia
sources.note: Identity, capital, extent, Deorham 577, Peonnum c. 658, Geraint and Ine 710, later history to 936.

sources.title: Battle of Peonnum
sources.note: Peonnum 658, annexation of eastern and central Somerset to the Parrett, border to 681-685, Bristol Channel.

notes:
Dumnonia (2 Cliopatria shapes, 602-709), budget 1-2 pages, two used.
SHAPE WAS NOT CHANGED BY CLIOPATRIA AT 658 OR 685 although the pages show two West Saxon advances; the correction is made with new keyframes dumnonia_602b (Somerset added before 658) and dumnonia_685 (Somerset removed). The Somerset geometry is Natural Earth's county, an approximation of 'eastern and central' and 'western' Somerset; confidence 2 for the regions, which are my reading. Pre-658 Dumnonia may have extended further; no page gives its eastern limit.
END 710 IS CLIOPATRIA'S AND THE BATTLE'S: the Dumnonia page has no end date and a long tail (rump state after 813-822, Donyarth died 875, Athelstan c. 936). Confidence 1. Cliopatria's Cornwall row (710-946) takes over; the Cornwall dossier belongs to another part (eu-11 'cornwall').
OVERLAP: the end year 710 is also Cornwall's first year (and Wessex's 710 shape); the rendering should let the successors win in 710.
Not opened: Geraint of Dumnonia, Battle of Hehil, Ine of Wessex, Kingdom of Wessex; the Isles of Scilly and Dorset are not mentioned as part of the post-Roman kingdom. No ruler list is documented.
